findings.title: Host cleanup requires a bound/absent producer scope even when only the setup observer exists
findings.trigger: Successful HOST_SETUP retains the observer window, then CreatePipe, output duplication, attribute-list allocation/initialization or CreateProcess fails before any producer exists.
source_trace: native_operation marks native_clean=false before HOST_SETUP. Successful setup records host_setup_ok and owns its observer, but host_bound and last_absent remain false until a later producer-installed probe.
host_main.done only attempts HOST_FINISH when host_bound&&last_absent. For an early no-producer failure it therefore skips the permitted unbound observer release.
Even adding that call alone is insufficient: observe(HOST_FINISH) requires host_observation, which requires identity_saved and probe_bound1. A legitimate unbound finish cannot mark native_clean.

native_clean stays false and the remaining host cleanup skips its own windows/module/class, retaining the observer and other local resources until external process cleanup despite no producer import being possible.

The same attempt-tracking contract matters for a partial HOST_SETUP: Native may retain the observer before an epoch/birth query error, and the Native receipt explicitly warns that error-frame window_owned is not a complete ownership ledger.
findings.evidence_boundary: The run truthfully fails/reports cleanup=false; this is an avoidable cleanup/progress defect, not fabricated success. It was found independently and also supplied by the parent for assessment. No failure was executed.
findings.requested_change: Reconcile the actual HOST_SETUP attempt when no producer was created, using permitted unbound HOST_FINISH and a distinct successful observer-only cleanup ledger that does not require or invent producer identity/model absence. Account for partial/late setup effects rather than relying only on an installed/bound proof. Keep the stronger bound fresh-absence path for the normal resource proof, and allow idempotent cleanup retries without replaying imports.

findings.title: Partial HOST_SETUP observer ownership still cannot reach or qualify unbound cleanup
findings.trigger: HOST_SETUP actually retains cross_host.window, then its root-epoch check or NtQueryInformationProcess(ProcessTimes) fails before the Native final output block. No producer has been created.
trace: native_operation sets native_clean=false before the setup call. Native owns a possible observer reference, but observe only sets host_setup_ok for a fully successful setup.
The new done branch still requires !created&&host_setup_ok. A partial setup error leaves host_setup_ok=false, host_bound=false and no producer, so permitted unbound HOST_FINISH is skipped.
The new unbound-finish observation branch also requires host_setup_ok and a complete queried birth/epoch. Calling finish alone therefore would not qualify local cleanup for the partial-setup case.

Native HOST_FINISH explicitly supports that unbound cleanup: its remembered root matches the caller's own root and it can release only the observer, with no producer/context/reader/model permission claim.

Consequently the observer/windows/module can remain unnecessarily retained until outer process cleanup. This is the partial-effect case already identified in the v1 assessment and the Native receipt's caller obligations.
findings.requested_change: Track/reconcile the acknowledged HOST_SETUP attempt, including partial effects, when no producer was created. Permit actual unbound observer cleanup and recognize its successful zero-owner result without requiring the failed setup queries or inventing model absence/producer SAFE. The run should still fail for the setup error. If exact partial identity cannot be represented by the current receipt, normalize/query it in the cleanup API rather than assuming no retained owner.
